binary.platform: Ubuntu Linux, Debug configuration; isolated XDG config/data/cache

model: Qwen3.5-9B-MTP Q4_K_M, served by llama.cpp with the existing CUDA runtime

protocol.backend: LlamaAgentBackend -> app MCP client -> restricted MCP stdio server -> Playwright Chromium
protocol.navigation_scope: allowlist of the three loopback fixture origins
protocol.unsafe_controls: host rejects any click whose control ID is not allowlisted for the current page
protocol.click_approval: test controller auto-approves only browser MCP clicks on disposable loopback fixtures
protocol.state_oracle: fixture HTTP /__state endpoint, independent of agent's text report

excluded_attempts: Early MCP/profile initialization attempts: runner setup was being debugged; not scored.

Two initial repeat-runner attempts: harness stopped the backend before switching project, so history reset was not guaranteed; corrected runner now switches project while backend is live and asserts an empty transcript.
One manual diagnostic run with reused conversation history: excluded as contaminated.
recommendation: Partial adoption as design principles only: keep host-side scope/unsafe-action guards and independent post-action state verification; do not promote a global transition/effects architecture based on this experiment. Improve permission-setting recognition and require verified state before reporting success.
limitations: Synthetic local websites, not native UI or AT-SPI2.
Three web origins were traversed by the real agent backend/MCP stack; no autonomous cross-application native desktop workflow was exercised.
Small sample; six exact end-to-end runs are not a general reliability estimate.
This compared objective-only autonomy to a guided sequence, not two planner architectures.
Only disposable loopback browser writes were auto-approved.
